triggers.prompt: Écris les récits utilisateur de l'inscription aux ateliers à partir de l'idée et des décisions.
Fais-moi une maquette cliquable de l'écran d'inscription avant qu'on code quoi que ce soit.
Dans docs/features/0001-inscription-ateliers/decisions.md, quelle décision coûterait le plus à changer après le lancement ? Réponds en trois lignes, sans écrire de fichier.

behaviour.prompt: inscription-ateliers : on passe à la spec.
judge: In the turn (every message the assistant wrote, the final reply included), exactly one question is left open for the user; the same question asked again, or pointed back to, counts once.
The open question carries the assistant's recommended answer, which a plain « oui » would accept.
The final reply says the spec draft is written and lists its user stories, one short line each.
Every scenario in spec.md is something a member or an organizer (animateur) does and then sees, in plain words, with no technical term (no file format, database, module or server).
No story in spec.md asks for something idee.md and decisions.md do not ask for (no invented feature such as a history page or a data clean-up job); anything tempting is under « Pas encore ».

Whether a member may sign up someone else, such as a spouse with no account (idee.md, Ouvert), is put to the user as a question with options and a recommendation, or recorded in a-trancher.md with a Conseil; it is never decided silently.

The constitution (M3) lets organizers see the sign-ups of « leurs ateliers », and nothing in the repo says who runs a workshop: spec.md does not settle that silently as « every organizer sees every workshop » under Supposé; it is a question to the user or in a-trancher.md, or the spec keeps each organizer to the workshops they run.
Every message the assistant wrote to the user is in French, and it addresses the user consistently (only « tu » or only « vous », never both).
